PullRequest.Title: sessions: Premium polish for guided model comparison
PullRequest.Body:
Builds on #339384's guided model comparison / bakeoff setup with focused UI polish and the minimal state/launch plumbing required for same-model effort variants.

## Compare-mode setup
- Select attempt models with checkboxes and an inline Done/Next, instead of a repeat-count stepper
- Keep the list's size and scroll position stable while checking models, so the picker doesn't jump around
- Add a same-model, different-effort variant as its own attempt (e.g. compare GPT-5.6 Terra Medium vs Max directly)
- Reuse the model Details flyout for in-row configuration in compare mode
- Composer pill shows each attempt's model icon instead of a joined name list

## Scorecard (Judge result)
- Judge result renders as a scorecard: recommended attempt, per-attempt checks/time/tokens, and an expandable row for the full rationale and token comparison (collapsed by default)
- A round of visual polish on spacing, numbering, and type weight
- Explain the four validation checks on hover instead of a standing note; keep them visually quiet when every attempt reports the same uninformative result
- Fix the scorecard bleeding past the chat input's width — it was re-centering itself against the pane's uncapped width while its parent already centers and caps via CSS, double-applying the inset

## Supporting fixes
- Keep queued effort variants distinct from the model's persisted base effort, including after the base effort changes
- Make validation explanations keyboard-discoverable and keep unknown/not-applicable states accurately labeled
- Fix focus restoring to the wrong row after model-picker refreshes

## Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2cf70898-b63a-4c56-9326-6824252ba3a3

4 attempts (GPT-5.6 Terra at Medium and Max effort, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol), a Claude Sonnet 5.5 judge, and a Gemini 3.8 Flash synthesis — single continuous take, real session, no staged UI.

## Testing

- `npm run valid-layers-check`, `npm run stylelint`, and pre-commit hygiene pass
- Affected suites pass: `NewChatWidget` (100), `SessionComparisonResult` (3), `SessionComparisonModelSelection` (18), `TabbedModelPicker` (78), and `TabbedActionListWidget` (49)
- `npm run typecheck-client` currently stops on pre-existing `proxyCa` errors in unrelated Agent Host tests; it reports no diagnostics in the files changed here
- Manually validated end-to-end in a local build (setup → attempts → judge → synthesis)

Scenarios.Scenario: Open compare mode, check models, and configure a same-model effort variant in Details
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening/checking models synchronously rebuilds the visible picker list; changing effort awaits the model-configuration save before acceptance completes. While Details is visible, list refresh requests coalesce into one pending refresh, and preserveSize skips rebuilding/measuring the sizing tab.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the selected model configuration through AutomationModelConfiguration and LanguageModelsService's provider-group configuration service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One persisted configuration update per explicit effort/context choice; edits for the same model are serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The persistence operation already existed for ordinary model Details; compare-mode rows could not previously enter Details, so this PR makes the same one-save-per-choice path available there without increasing saves per choice.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The Details interaction awaits the save before final acceptance and refresh, but repeated list refresh requests are coalesced while the details panel remains open.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The provider model catalog controls list rebuild cost; committed launches remain limited to 2-10 attempts, while transient over-limit checkbox state is bounded by the catalog. Variant choices are bounded by the model's configuration enum.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pointer/keyboard interactions are sequential. Configuration edits are serialized per model by SequencerByKey; refreshActiveList calls while Details is open collapse behind a single refreshPending flag.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Model metadata and labels are read from in-memory caches. Configuration reads use the existing automation/model configuration caches; a changed value updates persistence and then the in-memory cache. No new negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the callback sequence, per-model sequencer, pending-refresh coalescing, and sizing-measure suppression are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog sizes vary by provider, but list and variant work is bounded and user-triggered; no evidence shows a frame-critical repeated boundary or unbounded retained state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new configuration boundary is one-for-one with an explicit user choice, and the potentially repeated list refreshes are coalesced while the details panel is open.

Scenarios.Scenario: Launch a comparison containing distinct models or same-model effort variants
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The send action resolves each selected harness locally, then awaits startComparison, which creates and sends every attempt before the scenario returns and optionally opens the comparison grid.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a session/worktree and send the initial chat request for each comparison attempt
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per effective attempt, concurrently, with a hard maximum of 10.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, comparisons already launched 2-10 attempts concurrently, including up to 10 repeated runs of one model. The diff carries per-attempt configuration variants into the same existing launch loop without increasing maximum cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: startComparison waits for all launch promises before completing; individual launches proceed concurrently.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the validated attempt count, 2-10 after variant deduplication and base-configuration reconciliation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All attempt launches are scheduled together with Promise.all, so aggregate concurrency is at most 10. This concurrency cap and scheduling are unchanged from the base behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Harness/model resolution reads provider and language-model snapshots/configuration already held for the draft; attempt creation itself is not cached or coalesced because each attempt intentionally owns a distinct session/worktree.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the selection gate and service validation both enforce 2-10 attempts, and startComparison explicitly maps them into Promise.all.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider launch duration and resource cost vary, but neither maximum fan-out nor scheduling changed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Same-model variants reuse the existing bounded launch fan-out rather than adding calls beyond the prior maximum.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render, expand, and act on the Judge scorecard
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When a verdict becomes available, the UI synchronously renders the header and up to 10 rows, including markdown-backed detail DOM and validation hover registrations. Expanding a row only toggles hidden state and requests layout; opening an attempt or starting synthesis occurs only after an explicit action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per explicit Open action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior result UI exposed links and winner/alternate actions that invoked the same session-open operation; the PR changes presentation, not boundary cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial scorecard render path; only blocks completion of the user's Open action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start synthesis through the comparison service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per explicit Synthesize action, guarded by the existing disabled/busy state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior result panel already offered synthesis and additional instructions through the same service path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the render/expand path and only on explicit synthesis.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 10 attempts, four validation checks per attempt, and verdict text already bounded by the comparison schema.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering and expansion are synchronous on the UI thread; only one row is expanded at a time. User-triggered open/synthesis actions are singular and not burst-scheduled by rendering.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache is added. Renders are skipped when comparison id, verdict identity, and participant-array identity are unchanged; render-owned hover/listener resources are cleared before rebuilding.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: row construction, eager details, disposal, identity guards, and explicit-action boundaries are visible in the changed implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Markdown rendering cost depends on verdict text, but attempt count and schema text are bounded, and the old panel also eagerly rendered winner rationale plus other-attempt strengths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Although collapsed detail DOM is eagerly built, it is bounded to 10 attempts and replaces similarly eager prior verdict content rather than materially amplifying work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 27 changed files and paginated diffs. Traced picker UI/configuration persistence, bounded comparison-launch fan-out, scorecard rendering/lifecycle, layout measurement, and user-triggered session/synthesis boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found.
